newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sure can find cash for Chechen oil repairs.
newsitem.headline: Russia sure can find cash for Chechen oil repairs.

text.p: Russia is confident of raising the $2 million Chechnya says it needs to finish repairing the damaged oil pipeline running across Chechen territory, Fuel and Energy Minister Boris Nemtsov said on Friday.
He said that restoring the pipeline was the key to economic development in the war-ravaged breakaway region.
"We are not talking about a lot of money here." Nemtsov said. "Two million dollars for this kind of project is not a lot...We will find this from private business."
Nemtsov said no deals between Chechnya and Russia's oil pipeline monopoly had been signed yet, but he was confident there was a will on the Chechen side to reach an agreement.

"I think that there are people in Chechnya who understand the importance of this project for the economy of Chechnya. We are absolutely open to dealing with this," he told reporters after the signing ceremony of the Caspian Pipeline Consortium.
"If Chechnya is interested in the revival of its economy, then they should sit down here in Moscow and talk with (me and with Transneft), so that we can get down to work quicker."

Chechnya's highest oil official said on Monday that repairs to the Chechen section of a pipeline running from the Caspian Sea to Russian export outlets in the Black Sea could be finished in 20 to 30 days if $2 million financing was found.
Khozhakhmed Yarikhanov, president of the Southern Oil Company, or YUNKO, said that a third of the repair work on the line had been completed by the beginning of the week.
Some early oil produced by international consortium Azerbaijan International Operating Co (AIOC) is due to move along the Russian pipeline route which passes through Chechnya.
AIOC has a deal with Transneft to carry its oil to Novorossiisk by the beginning of October.
